utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone. I would like to ask the Court Deputy to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-9-A, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Simic, are you in a position to listen to the proceedings and to understand them? Okay. Now we'd like to have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon. Appearing for the Prosecution is myself, Norman Farrell, and appearing with me is Ms. Barbara Goy and Ms. Lourdes Galicia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'm turning to the Defence of Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Mr. Pantelic for Dr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Peter Murphy for the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Pursuant to Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules, a Status Conference has to be held within 120 days following the filing of the notice of appeal and then every 120 days to give the opportunity to the person waiting for the appeal proceedings the possibility of raising any questions relating to the appeal. In this case, Mr. Simic filed his notice of appeal against the judgement on the 17th of October, 2003. The submissions related to the appeal have been filed, and we are currently gathered together for the third Status Conference of this appeals procedure. The aim of this Status Conference, as you know, is, among other things, to allow Mr. Simic to raise any concerns he might have regarding his detention and his mental and physical state. Mr. Simic, would you or your counsel raise anything before the Chamber, any problems related to your detention or to your state of health? Mr. Simic, you have the floor. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my health is good. I have no complaints. I have no complaints against the conditions of detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm glad to hear it. Mr. Pantelic, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I don't have anything to add regarding this specific matter. We're here to discuss our motion for provisional release.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We'll come to that later. I'm sure you have received this information. In this case, the submissions related to the appeals procedures have been filed. I have noted the filing of a notice of appeal amended, the amended notice of appeal on the 22nd of September, 2004, and the public version of the brief in reply of the Prosecution that was filed yesterday. Therefore, the Appeals Chamber will be in a position to determine its position in the case in the following months. Before informing counsel for Mr. Simic about the outcome of the motion filed by Mr. Simic I would like to present my condolences to Mr. Simic on the occasion of the demise of his father. This being said, with regards to the urgent motion filed by Mr. Simic for provisional release in order to allow him to attend a memorial service for his father, the Appeals Chamber has decided to rule in favour of Mr. Simic and will allow him to attend the memorial services organised on the 4th of November, 2004. However, the Appeals Chamber has decided not to grant the entirety of the period for provisional release requested and decided to allow him a period from the 3rd to the 7th of November, 2004. The reasons for this decision will be submitted, will be communicated to the parties very soon. With regards to the procedure, I would also like to stress that the motion filed by Franko Simatovic for access to the documents related to the Bosanski Samac case is still pending before the Chamber. As far as I am concerned, I don't have any other issues to address. I would like to ask the parties if they have any comments or any questions they would like to raise. Mr. Farrell, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No, there are no comments nor further questions on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, firstly may I, on behalf of Dr. Simic, thank the Appeals Chamber for the ruling on the motion for provisional release. And the only other matter, Your Honour: I wonder whether the Appeals Chamber is in a position at this time to indicate approximately when we may expect to have oral argument on the merits of the appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No date has been set yet, but you will be notified of that as soon as the Chamber is in a position to set a date. Thank you. Is there any other issue you would like to raise? Is there any other comment you would like to make?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Since there aren't any other issues to consider, this Status Conference is adjourned. The Status Conference is adjourned.
